lesson.title: Modeling Linear Systems
intro: A system of equations can be used to model situations where two quantities are related in different ways.
Each equation represents a relationship between variables.
Solving the system finds the values that satisfy both equations at the same time.

workedExample.problem: Two taxi companies charge different starting fees and per-mile rates. Their cost equations are y = 2x + 3 and y = 4x − 5.
steps: Each equation represents a cost model.
Graph both equations on the same coordinate plane.
The point where the graphs intersect represents when both companies cost the same amount.
workedExample.answer: The intersection point represents the break-even point.

questions.prompt:
Alex had $1.70 in nickels and dimes on his desk. There were 25 coins in all.

If n represents the number of nickels and d represents the number of dimes, which system of equations models the situation?
questions.explanation: The total number of coins is n + d = 25. The total value in dollars is 0.05n + 0.10d = 1.70.

questions.prompt:
Courtney went to a coffee shop to purchase lattes and donuts for her friends.

One day she spent $15.50 on four lattes and two donuts. The next day she spent $18.10 on three lattes and five donuts.

If x represents the cost of one latte and y represents the cost of one donut, which system correctly models the situation?
